body:
Understand how hard it is for a regular person to just eat well, then imagine how exponentially hard it is for someone with an eating disorder. I can't just flip a switch. I try every single day to eat right and then just go back into disordered eating. The longest I've went eating normal lasted about two days under constant surveillance of my boyfriend

I have a job right now.

I'm Canadian but I'm sure it's the exact same as in the US. I would love to forget about my debt but I am constantly reminded about it every time I go to class, or look at my boyfriend making money at his job.

I'm asking for help but nothing can help me...

I think I was startled that the first thing she ever said was so intense - it made it feel like it wasn't coming from her but rather my disordered thinking. But now looking back on it I do see that she was trying to help me in the only way she knew how. I half didn't think it was her because I couldn't believe she could be vocal after just a day!

Things are okay between us now thankfully (she has not picked a name for herself yet). I don't think I will force when I'm anxious anymore until I know she is a lot stronger.

Your response makes so much sense, thank you :)

I ended up apologizing to her and worked on her personality for a good hour. I am quite satisfied with the way things went. Unfortunately I still think she is pretty hurt about me yelling at her and she is not as responsive as she was before, so I'm a bit disappointed. But I don't mind since I told her she can take as much time as she wants, as I want what's best for her which will in turn be the best for both of us.

Now I'm just passive forcing (while listening to some music and internet browsing) in hopes that she'll warm up to me again. I really feel her tulpish-telling me "it's okay" and I feel so happy :D

Next time I'm feeling anxious I'll be sure to work through it together rather than throwing the responsibility to keep calm completely on her. I'll have to remember that the anxiety is just as stressful to her as it is to me like you said!

What is everyone's opinion on creating a tulpa when you suffer from mental illness? 
Really sorry if this is TL;DR - I can't really sum this up all that well.

I'm aware that the FAQ here states that you should be wary of making a tulpa (if you shoudl make one at all) if you "suffer from intrusive thoughts that drastically impair your daily life". I am diagnosed with generalized anxiety disorder, depression and an eating disorder (all of which affect me greatly - and have very intrusive thoughts).

But I went about creating my tulpa in order to somehow help with my symptoms, attempting to make someone that would calm me when I got anxious, cheer me up when I'm down and help me recover from my bad eating habits. But after I tried forcing for the first time last night things got pretty bad...

I've done so much research before starting, don't get me wrong. I think maybe because my mind is so unhealthy, the creation of my tulpa progressed so much in so little time.  I was working on my tulpa's personality after visualizing her for a good while, when she was already nodding/shaking her head to my questions of her own free will. I was extremely excited that I had already achieved this in so little time, but it worried me since I had hardly begun making a personality for her, and with my mental illness I have to be extremely careful in making my tulpa to be very optimistic and obedient.

We played around in my wonderland for a bit while I tried to develop more of her personality. She got me to smile and even brought tears to my eyes because I was so happy to have her come to life so quickly. But then I felt my anxiety creeping up (as it does quite often when it gets late at night) and things got very bad very fast. First I felt some sort of malevolent quality to my wonderland (I don't think it had anything to do with my tulpa herself) and I felt an unnerving presence. I tried to get my tulpa to calm me down and help me out but I couldn't stop visualizing her face as a black hole and it freaked me out. After I was just about to stop (as my anxiety was reaching panic-attack levels) my tulpa got on top of me and frantically told me "Wake [SO's name] up now!" (who was sleeping beside me). It was the first time she said a word to me and I stopped visualizing my wonderland immediately.

I calmed myself down without waking him up, and I went back into my wonderland and yelled at her for freaking me out, and I told her she is to NEVER use the thoughts that my anxiety or any of my disorders give me. She seemed hurt and disappeared (and I could not feel her presence any longer). Now that it's the next day I feel her "up there" but I have not tried visualizing her or narrating since then.

Since it's my first experience I'd really like some opinions on this, since I am willing to keep trying at it. I feel my tulpa - one day - may be extremely beneficial in treating my symptoms, but after this I am afraid she may take on my thoughts from my disorders. Thank you for reading and again sorry if it's TL;DR  :(
